edition_notes: French-language rulebook, © 2020 Blue Orange Edition, © 2017 Dolphin Hat Games LLC; 2-8 players, ages 8+, about 10 minutes; 64 cards.

items.rule: Shuffle the cards and deal them face down to all players according to player count.
With 2, 3, 4 or 5 players, each player receives 12 cards.
With 6 players, each player receives 10 cards.
With 7 or 8 players, each player receives 8 cards.
Leftover cards are returned to the box.
Players do not look at their cards; each forms a face-down personal draw pile in front of them.
The player who dealt the cards is the first player of the first round.
The game is played in a series of rounds until a player achieves the goal of the game.
The first player of the round takes the top card of their pile, places it face up in the center of the table and says "Taco".
Play continues clockwise: each next player flips the top card of their pile onto the center pile and says the next word in the sequence.
The word sequence is always Taco, Chat, Bouc, Cheese, Pizza, then repeats (Taco, Chat...), continuing across players without restarting.
Each card must be flipped face up toward the other players, not toward oneself.
A match occurs when the card revealed is the same as the word the player says (e.g., a Pizza card played while saying "Pizza"); then all players slap the center pile as fast as possible.
The last player to slap the pile (hand on top) takes all cards in the center pile and adds them face down under their draw pile; that player starts the next round.
When a special card (Gorille, Marmotte, Narval) is revealed, all players must perform its action before slapping the pile.
Gorille: all players beat their chest.
Marmotte: all players hit the table with both hands.
Narval: all players place both hands above their head forming a horn.
A player who does the wrong action or is the last to slap on a special card takes the whole center pile and puts it under their draw pile.
A player who slaps at the wrong time, or starts to slap and retracts, loses their turn and takes the whole center pile under their draw pile.
A player who forgets what to say, says the wrong word, or fails to notice it is their turn takes the whole center pile under their draw pile; play must keep a brisk pace.
A player who obviously tries to peek at their card before playing it loses their turn and takes the whole center pile under their draw pile.
A player who has played all their cards must still say the next word on their turn and must be FIRST to slap on a match or special card to win.
If the word announced matches the card already visible in the center (not the one just played), it is not a match and the round continues normally.
If a player with no cards left is not first to slap, a new round starts and they keep playing until they succeed in slapping first.
The game ends when a player has no draw pile left and is first to slap the pile on a match or a special card.
There is no point scoring; the aim is to get rid of all of your cards.
The winner is the first player who has no personal draw pile left and is first to slap the pile on a match or after a special card appears.
